external_entities.name: sensor node
external_entities.description: A deployed sensor node installed at a customer site that publishes readings and polls for firmware updates.
external_entities.source_excerpt: We have a few thousand sensor nodes installed on customer sites.
external_entities.notes: The nodes are outside the organisation's physical control.

external_entities.name: field technician
external_entities.description: A technician who services sensor nodes over a local serial console.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Field technicians service nodes over a local serial console.

external_entities.name: fleet operator
external_entities.description: An operator who views telemetry dashboards from the corporate network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network, signed in with company SSO.

processes.name: device gateway
processes.description: An MQTT broker running on GKE that accepts readings from sensor nodes and forwards them to Pub/Sub.
processes.source_excerpt: the device gateway, which is an MQTT broker we run on GKE
processes.notes: The gateway is exposed to the internet. Nodes authenticate with a fleet-wide pre-shared key that has not been rotated since deployment.

processes.name: telemetry normalizer
processes.description: A Python consumer in the analytics network that picks up readings and writes them into the telemetry lake.
processes.source_excerpt: the telemetry normalizer, a Python consumer in our analytics network

data_stores.name: device registry
data_stores.description: A Firestore registry used to check a device key and identify which customer a node belongs to.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The gateway looks up the device in a device registry (Firestore) to check the key and to find out which customer the node belongs to.

data_stores.name: Pub/Sub
data_stores.description: A messaging service onto which accepted readings are forwarded for consumption by the telemetry normalizer.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub

data_stores.name: telemetry lake
data_stores.description: A BigQuery data store containing sensor telemetry, site addresses, and occupancy patterns.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The lake has site addresses and occupancy patterns in it, so it is customer data.

data_stores.name: firmware bucket
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket from which sensor nodes poll firmware images.
data_stores.source_excerpt: nodes poll a Cloud Storage bucket for a new image and install what they find.
data_stores.notes: The bucket is public read. It is unknown whether nodes verify an image signature before installing it.

data_flows.name: publish readings
data_flows.description: A sensor node publishes readings to the device gateway.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Each node publishes readings over MQTT to the device gateway

data_flows.name: look up device
data_flows.description: The device gateway looks up the device record to check the key and identify the customer.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The gateway looks up the device in a device registry (Firestore) to check the key and to find out which customer the node belongs to.

data_flows.name: forward readings
data_flows.description: The device gateway forwards accepted readings onto Pub/Sub.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub

data_flows.name: pick up readings
data_flows.description: The telemetry normalizer picks up readings from Pub/Sub.
data_flows.source_excerpt: picked up by the telemetry normalizer

data_flows.name: write telemetry
data_flows.description: The telemetry normalizer writes readings into the telemetry lake.
data_flows.source_excerpt: which writes them into the telemetry lake in BigQuery

data_flows.name: poll image
data_flows.description: A sensor node polls the firmware bucket for a new image.
data_flows.source_excerpt: nodes poll a Cloud Storage bucket for a new image

data_flows.name: service node
data_flows.description: A field technician services a sensor node over its local serial console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Field technicians service nodes over a local serial console.
data_flows.notes: I don't know what authentication that console has, if any.

data_flows.name: view dashboards
data_flows.description: A fleet operator views dashboards using BigQuery from the corporate network.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network, signed in with company SSO.

trust_boundaries.name: customer sites
trust_boundaries.description: Customer-controlled sites where the deployed sensor nodes are installed.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: sensor nodes installed on customer sites

trust_boundaries.name: analytics network
trust_boundaries.description: The analytics network in which the telemetry normalizer runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the telemetry normalizer, a Python consumer in our analytics network

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network from which fleet operators access dashboards.

assumptions.assumption: The customer sites are controlled by customers other than the platform operator.
assumptions.basis: The sensor nodes are installed on customer sites and are outside the organisation's physical control.

assumptions.assumption: The device gateway presents a non-web interface because it is described as an MQTT broker.
assumptions.basis: The device gateway is explicitly described as an MQTT broker.

assumptions.assumption: The telemetry normalizer presents a non-web interface because it is described as a Python consumer.
assumptions.basis: The telemetry normalizer is explicitly described as a Python consumer.

assumptions.assumption: The device registry contains credentials and personal data.
assumptions.basis: It stores or checks a device key and identifies which customer a node belongs to.

assumptions.assumption: The device registry is confidential.
assumptions.basis: It contains a device key and customer association, which are sensitive credentials and customer data.

assumptions.assumption: Pub/Sub carries personal data.
assumptions.basis: Accepted readings are forwarded onto Pub/Sub and the resulting telemetry includes site addresses and occupancy patterns identified as customer data.

assumptions.assumption: Pub/Sub is confidential.
assumptions.basis: It carries readings that become customer data in the telemetry lake.

assumptions.assumption: The telemetry lake contains personal data.
assumptions.basis: The lake contains site addresses and occupancy patterns and is explicitly described as customer data.

assumptions.assumption: The telemetry lake is confidential.
assumptions.basis: Site addresses and occupancy patterns are customer data whose disclosure can harm or identify customers.

assumptions.assumption: The firmware image is business-critical data.
assumptions.basis: The bucket stores firmware images used to update the deployed sensor fleet.

assumptions.assumption: The sensor node carries personal data in the readings it publishes.
assumptions.basis: The node publishes readings that flow into telemetry containing site addresses and occupancy patterns identified as customer data.

assumptions.assumption: The device gateway handles personal data.
assumptions.basis: It accepts and forwards sensor readings that become customer data.

assumptions.assumption: The telemetry normalizer handles personal data.
assumptions.basis: It picks up sensor readings and writes them into the customer-data telemetry lake.
